'''Elisabeth Giacobino''' (born April 2, 1946) is a French physicist specialized in [[laser physics]], [[nonlinear optics]], [[quantum optics]] and [[Superfluidity|super-fluidity]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Elisabeth Giacobino {{!}} Quantum Optics group|url=http://www.lkb.upmc.fr/quantumoptics/project/elisabeth-giacobino/|access-date=2020-06-05|website=www.lkb.upmc.fr|language=en-GB|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200605204207/http://www.lkb.upmc.fr/quantumoptics/project/elisabeth-giacobino/|archive-date=2020-06-05|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/uploads/tx_leopublication/Neugewaehlte_Mitglieder_2009_03.pdf|title=Leopoldina – Neugewählte Mitglieder 2009|publisher=Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher Leopoldina e. V. – Nationale Akademie der Wissenschaften|year=2010|location=Halle (Saale), Deutschland|page=36|access-date=2020-06-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304210903/http://www.leopoldina.org/uploads/tx_leopublication/Neugewaehlte_Mitglieder_2009_03.pdf|archive-date=2016-03-04|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Professor Elisabeth Giacobino|url=https://www.cqc2t.org/professor-elisabeth-giacobino/|access-date=2020-06-08|website=CQC2T|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608142707/https://www.cqc2t.org/professor-elisabeth-giacobino/|archive-date=2020-06-08|url-status=live}}</ref> She is one of the pioneers of quantum optics and quantum information.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=NANOP 2016 – Plenary speakers|url=https://premc.org/nanop2016/plenary-speakers/|access-date=2020-06-17|website=PremC|language=en-GB}}</ref> She graduated from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] ([[Pierre and Marie Curie University|Paris VI]]) and started working at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]], where she has spent the majority of her professional career.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /> She has been an invited professor at [[New York University]] and [[University of Auckland]].<ref name=":4" /> She has over 230 publications and over 110 invited presentations in international conferences. She has been the coordinator of four European projects and is a member of [[:fr:Académie Léopoldine|Academia Leopoldina]] as well as a fellow member of the [[European Physical Society]], the [[European Optical Society]] and the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]].<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" />

== Education and career ==
Elisabeth studied from 1965 to 1969 at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]], then in 1969 she got her [[Agrégation]] in [[Physical Sciences]] and in 1976 she got her [[Doctorate Degree]] in Physics,<ref name=":0" /> specializing in [[Atomic Physics]] and [[Optics]] at the [[Université Paris VI]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Elisabeth Giacobino|url=http://www.fet11.eu/programme-committee-member/26-elisabeth-giacobino.html|access-date=2020-06-06|website=www.fet11.eu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160716054430/http://www.fet11.eu/programme-committee-member/26-elisabeth-giacobino.html|archive-date=2016-07-16|url-status=live}}</ref> Her PhD Thesis was on the "Study of Excited Neon Levels by Laser Spectroscopy without Doppler Effect".<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Etude des niveaux excités du néon par spectroscopie laser sans effet Doppler|url=https://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/tel-00011824|publisher=Université Pierre et Marie Curie – Paris VI|date=1976-04-15|degree=phdthesis|language=fr|first=Elisabeth|last=Giacobino|access-date=2020-06-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606225311/https://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/tel-00011824|archive-date=2020-06-06|url-status=live}}</ref> From 1969 to 1976 she worked as a Junior Researcher (''Attaché de Recherche'') at the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]] ("''[[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]]''", CNRS). Then, from 1976 to 1982 she worked as a full researcher at the CNRS. From 1982 to 1983 she was an invited professor at [[New York University]]. From 1982 to 2002 she worked as a research director at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]. From 2003 to 2006 she was the Director of Research at the [[Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation|Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Research]]. Then from 2006 to 2011 she returned as Research Director at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]. From 2011 to the present she is a Research Director Emerite at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Présence du CNRS... Recherche et Université|url=https://webcast.in2p3.fr/video/presence-du-cnrs-recherche-et-universite|access-date=2020-06-06|website=CC-Webcast|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606225621/https://webcast.in2p3.fr/video/presence-du-cnrs-recherche-et-universite|archive-date=2020-06-06|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=GIACOBINO Elisabeth – Auteurs – Canal-U|url=https://www.canal-u.tv/auteurs/giacobino_elisabeth|access-date=2020-06-06|website=www.canal-u.tv|date=3 August 2000 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606231815/https://www.canal-u.tv/auteurs/giacobino_elisabeth|archive-date=2020-06-06|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":4" />

As part of her involvement to advocate for the future of young [[physicist]]s, in 2008 she was part of a group of scientists that made the written statement ''La situation des femmes physiciennes en France'', during the Third International Conference on Women in Physics (ICWIP2008) on which they analyzed the current situation of female physicists in France and made recommendations to improve the current state.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Thibault|first1=Catherine|last2=Pépin|first2=Anne|last3=Ducloy|first3=Martial|last4=Giacobino|first4=Élisabeth|last5=Leduc|first5=Michèle|author5-link=Michèle Leduc|date=2009-05-01|title=La situation des femmes physiciennes en France|url=https://www.refletsdelaphysique.fr/articles/refdp/abs/2009/02/refdp200914p24/refdp200914p24.html|journal=Reflets de la Physique|language=fr|issue=14|pages=24–26|doi=10.1051/refdp/2009011|issn=1953-793X|access-date=2020-06-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180605000907/https://www.refletsdelaphysique.fr/articles/refdp/abs/2009/02/refdp200914p24/refdp200914p24.html|archive-date=2018-06-05|url-status=live|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Research and contributions ==
Elisabeth Giacobino has had a prolific career with over 230 publications and over 110 invited presentations in international conferences. Over the last 50 years, her [[research]] contributions has been to several areas of research. From 1970 to 1987 she worked on [[Spectroscopy|laser spectroscopy]] and [[Doppler-free spectroscopy|Doppler-free]] two-[[photon]] [[spectroscopy]] in rare [[gas]]es and alkali vapours, collisional effects, [[Non-linear effects|nonlinear effect]] and [[Optical bistability|optical bi-stability]]. From 1985 to 1995 she worked mostly in [[quantum optics]]. In 1987 she demonstrated, for the first time, two-beam squeezing generated by a [[parametric oscillator]].<ref name=":1" /> From 1990 to 1998 her research focused on noise studies in [[Laser diode|semi-conductor lasers]] and in [[Microlaser|micro-lasers]]. From 1990–2003 she worked on [[quantum state]] generation with [[Ultracold atom|cold atoms]]. In 1995, with the use of a cloud of laser-cooled atoms, she proposed a new method to generate [[Squeezed states of light|squeezed light]]; and in 2003, a new method to generate entangled beams of light.<ref name=":1" /> In 2005 she started working on [[electromagnetically induced transparency]], light matter entanglement and development of quantum memories in atomic ensembles. After demonstrating the capability of [[vapour]]s to store [[quantum state]]s of light, she started working on quantum memory register based on a cold atom cloud.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Giacobino|first=Elisabeth|date=29 October 2018|title=Is quantum computing becoming a reality?|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jzX6epOvi_A|access-date=8 June 2020|website=YouTube}}</ref><ref name=":6" />

From 1998 to the present she has been working on semiconductor microcavities and on the study of [[Nonlinear system|nonlinear]] and [[Bistability|bi-stable]] behavior.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Citation|title=JQI Seminar 5/5/14 – Elisabeth Giacobino|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xOPV5UMPHsA|language=en|access-date=2020-06-08}}</ref> In passive semiconductor microcavities, she demonstrated, for the first time, the emission of squeezed light and correlated beams.<ref name=":1" /> From 2001 to the present she has been involved in the studies of semiconductor nano-crystals, specifically on [[Single-photon source|single photon generation]] and cavity [[quantum electrodynamics]] (QED) effects.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Giacobino|first=Elisabeth|date=12 June 2019|title=Quantum fluids of light|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mr47cQZoT3w|access-date=8 June 2020|website=YouTube}}</ref> In this line of research, concerning semiconductor systems, she studied intensity [[quantum noise]] in [[Laser diode|semiconductor lasers]] and explained how to reduced it.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" />

== Research management ==
She was the coordinator of four [[European Research Council|European Projects]] and a partner with several of them.<ref name=":1" /> She has held several positions in the management of research in France, specially at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) and at the [[Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation|Ministry of Higher Education and Research]].<ref name=":1" /> From 1992 to 1995 she was appointed expert for the [[Atomic physics|atomic]] and [[molecular physics]], and [[optics]] at the [[Mathematics]] and [[Physics]] Department of CNRS. From 1994 to 1997 she was the deputy director of the [[Kastler–Brossel Laboratory|Kastle Brossel Laboratory]]. From 1995 to 1999 she was the deputy director of the Mathematics and Physics Department at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]. From 1995 to 2000 she was appointed expert for the [[European Commission]] as a member of the Physics Panel for individual ([[Marie Curie Fellowship|Marie Curie) fellowships]] and in 2000 chairperson for the Training Sites. From 1996 to 2001 she was an elected member of the "''Conseil National des Universités''". From 1997 to 2001 she was a member of the Commission of Specialist from ''l'[[Paris Diderot University|Université Paris VII]]''. From 1999–2001 she was the Director of the [[Kastler–Brossel Laboratory|Kastler Brossel Laboratory]]. From 2001 to 2002 she was the director of the Mathematics and Physics Department at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]]. From 2002 to 2006 she was the General Director of Research at the [[Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Innovation|Ministry of Higher Education and Research]]. From 2006 to 2010 she was the Head of Interdisciplinary Programs at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and Advisor to the Director General at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" />

From 2006 to the present she has worked as the President of the National Network for [[Complex system|Complex Systems]]. From 2009 to 2012 she was the chair of the jury for Natural Sciences at the ''[[Institut Universitaire de France]]'' (IUF). From 2006 to the present she has worked as the President of the [[:fr:Institut d'optique Graduate School|Institute of Optics]], Graduate School. From 2015 to the present she has been an advisor to the ANR, the [[Agence nationale de la recherche|French National Research Agency]], in the areas of Quantum Technologies.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4" />
